#5227. Amundi Puts a European Equity Fund Share Class on Ethereum

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Amundi has launched a tokenised share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 equity index fund on public Ethereum, working with CACEIS. It is a real fund share-class initiative, not a claim that all 600 constituent stocks are individually trading as permissionless tokens around the clock.

One of Europe’s biggest asset managers has moved a conventional index product into the world of tokenised fund units. In a November 2026 announcement, Amundi said a new share class of its Core STOXX Europe 600 strategy had been issued on public Ethereum, using infrastructure developed with CACEIS.

That matters because asset tokenisation is often discussed in abstract terms. Here, the starting point is an existing diversified European equity strategy and a new way of recording or distributing interests in it.

Amundi’s Core STOXX Europe 600 tracks a broad European equity benchmark. What the firm has announced is a tokenised share class of the fund. It has not said that every underlying company has issued new public blockchain shares or that investors can automatically trade each of those stocks at any hour.

The distinction is fundamental. In a fund structure, an investor owns units governed by the fund’s legal terms. The fund, in turn, holds or tracks the underlying basket according to its mandate. Tokenising the unit can change the infrastructure used for issuance, transfer or recordkeeping without changing the basic economic exposure of the underlying investment strategy.

The company says the traditional distribution model remains available. The Ethereum-linked share class is integrated into the existing operating model rather than replacing the fund’s conventional administration overnight.

Amundi highlights potential benefits including operational efficiency, quicker settlement, transparency and improved distribution. These are plausible advantages of shared digital records, but each depends on regulatory acceptance, custodianship, identity controls and the systems connecting a blockchain to conventional fund administration.

CACEIS’s role is important because a token cannot, by itself, maintain every legal and administrative function expected of a regulated fund. Shareholder rights, transfer restrictions, reconciliation, accounting and redemption procedures still require well-defined responsible parties.

The effort follows earlier Amundi work involving tokenised money-market products and subscriptions using stablecoins. That progression suggests the asset manager is testing multiple financial use cases rather than assuming one technology will immediately replace existing market infrastructure.

NewsBTC recently examined the NYSE’s planned tokenised securities venue and its transfer-agent partners. The US exchange’s programme and Amundi’s European fund are distinct, but both underline the importance of ownership records and operational plumbing. A blockchain timestamp alone does not resolve an investor-rights question.

The most useful measurements will be actual eligible investors using the new share class, the cost and speed of subscriptions and redemptions, secondary-transfer rules and how issuers handle corporate actions and compliance. Amundi has not published enough in the cited announcement to quantify all these outcomes.

There is also no reason to equate demand for tokenised fund units with a guaranteed effect on ETH’s market price. Transaction fees and onchain activity are one component of a much larger network economy, and adoption can grow without a direct one-for-one connection to token valuations.

The development is meaningful because it involves an established asset manager applying public blockchain infrastructure to an actual investment product. The next chapter is operational evidence: whether the new representation makes fund ownership simpler, cheaper or more accessible without compromising the protections investors expect.

In the last 24 hours alone, HyperLabs distributed over 179K HYPE worth about $14.50 million to six team members’ wallets. The distribution was uneven, with these tokens unstaked about two days ago. These wallets are the ones to watch for potential selling pressure.

However, the protocol’s burn mechanism provided a counterweight to the new supply hitting the markets. Over 21K HYPE, worth about $1.64 million, was bought and burned at an average price of $77.93.

Meanwhile, a subsidiary of Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (HSI) filed an application with the U.S Commodities Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to become a Futures commission merchant. At the time of writing, the filing was still awaiting approval.

If approved, U.S clients could trade Perpetual Futures on a regulated platform, though there will be no definitive timing just yet. The HSI, meanwhile, reported $620.6 million in profits for the third quarter of this year. An approval would increase these profits in the next few sessions.

On the price charts, HYPE entered a downtrend, even though it was still confined in a sideways range. After Paradigm’s unstaking, the altcoin fell to around $80 and went on to break down the support. It established a low of $76 before entering a short pullback to the upside.

At press time, HYPE was trading towards the broken support at $80, potentially for a retest. Technically, it suggested that bears were in control, with the CMF showing capital flight as its reading stood at -0.19.

This reading was reinforced by the Directional Movement Index (DMI), with its three main lines all pointing south.

In short, HYPE has been facing conflicting signals lately.

Institutions have been unstaking despite looming regulatory clarity. Therefore, HYPE could hold above $75, a support level that has been in place for the last two months if bullish signals prevail.

Otherwise, if the level breaks down, it would set a precedent for demand zones at $70, $60, or lower.

#5223. DarkSword iPhone Exploit Drains $4M in Crypto Theft

Home » Crypto Market News » DarkSword iPhone Exploit Drains $4M in Crypto Theft

Zero-click browser vulnerability drains millions from unpatched devices by targeting stored recovery phrases.

A silent zero-click exploit chain targeting iPhones has drained more than $4 million in cryptocurrency across 365 TRON wallets, according to a report by Bitquery.

Dubbed DarkSword, the sophisticated attack kit compromises unpatched iOS devices through Safari—allowing hackers to extract private keys and seed phrases without requiring a single transaction signature or app download.

DarkSword, a kit for hacking iPhones, chains six iOS vulnerabilities to hijack devices running iOS 18.4 through 18.7. It compromises vulnerable iPhones through malicious websites opened in Apple’s Safari browser.

The exploit chain combines multiple security vulnerabilities to gain access to sensitive device information without requiring users to download an application or authorize a wallet transaction.

Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), together with cybersecurity firms Lookout and iVerify, published technical analyses of the exploit on March 18, 2026. Their findings describe an attack chain capable of accessing passwords, messages, and cryptocurrency wallet information stored in Apple’s Keychain.

A separate investigation by cybersecurity firm Censys identified modules targeting 18 cryptocurrency wallet applications. The toolkit can reportedly search photos and note-taking applications for recovery phrases, potentially exposing wallets whose credentials were stored on the device.

Targeted applications reportedly include MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, and Coinbase. The vulnerability lies in the iPhone’s operating system rather than the individual wallet applications.

Unlike conventional phishing attacks, DarkSword does not necessarily require victims to connect their wallets or approve suspicious transactions. Attackers who obtain a private key or recovery phrase can use another device to sign and broadcast transactions.

Bitquery’s investigation identified a network of 43 collection addresses connected through a shared fee wallet. The addresses received funds from 365 TRON wallets between October 5 and November 4.

The investigation found that at least $4.06 million in USDT was transferred. Of the 365 wallets affected, the median loss was $1,029. Eight wallets lost more than $100,000 each, accounting for 63% of the total USDT losses. The attackers reportedly sent small amounts of TRX to victims’ wallets shortly before draining their balances.

Bitquery traced the transfers back to an initial transaction whose amount and timing matched those of a publicly reported iPhone theft. However, blockchain records cannot reveal which devices or wallet applications individual victims were using.

Apple has released security updates addressing the vulnerabilities used by DarkSword. Google recommends installing the latest available iOS version or enabling Apple’s Lockdown Mode when an update is not possible.

Changing wallet passwords or revoking token approvals is not sufficient if attackers already possess the recovery phrase. A compromised seed requires generating a new one and transferring the assets.

DarkSword device-level attacks bypass wallet approval checks, so exposed seed phrases can lead to total loss without a single signature from the victim.

TL;DR: Coinbase’s November 5 product update describes an integrated set of services for token issuers, from sales and distribution through listings, custody and liquidity. It cites Monad, Ethena and Hyperliquid as examples, but the examples are company-selected and do not eliminate the risks or regulatory limits facing token projects.

For a blockchain project, issuing a token may be the relatively easy part. Finding real users, managing custody, listing on exchanges and supporting institutional trading each introduce complicated operational decisions. In a November 5 announcement, Coinbase presented those tasks as parts of one integrated platform for token issuers.

The pitch is straightforward: use fewer separate service providers and reduce the number of operational handoffs. For developers and investors, the interesting question is how much of that convenience comes from genuine technical integration and how much reflects the commercial advantage of a large incumbent bundling its own services.

Coinbase pointed to a public MON token sale involving an affiliate of Monad Foundation, describing more than 85,000 purchasers in over 70 countries. It said the token now has more than 150,000 unique traders and $7.2 billion in spot volume on its platform. Those are company-reported measures from a chosen example, not a representative result for every issuer that uses similar services.

With Ethena, Coinbase described a relationship that expanded from token-management tools into institutional custody, wallets and trading. It also cited a USDC-related product and hundreds of millions of dollars in new deposits. For Hyperliquid, the company emphasised its role in deploying USDC treasury infrastructure and supporting large transfers.

The three examples involve different business models, market structures and needs. They demonstrate possible uses for the platform, but readers should not assume that success in one project translates directly into another token’s demand or risk profile.

Bundling services can remove duplicate work for a project team. One integration may simplify onboarding, compliance coordination and support. It can also make changing suppliers harder if critical functions become dependent on the same provider.

A token issuer should examine who legally controls assets at every stage, what happens if a service is paused, how withdrawal requests are handled and whether exchanges and custodians have the right safeguards for each market. Convenience is not a substitute for operational resilience.

That issue connects to NewsBTC’s earlier coverage of Coinbase’s restrictions on certain stablecoins for EEA customers. An exchange service can be available in one region but restricted in another without changing the underlying token network. Eligibility and local regulation remain part of any credible launch plan.

Coinbase also said it is broadening work around tokenised equities and access to private markets. Those plans should be distinguished from products already live and from securities that may require additional identity or jurisdictional checks.

The practical questions go beyond transaction volume: what are the total fees, the terms of custody, the geographic eligibility limits, support commitments and data-portability arrangements? What functions can an issuer replace if its needs change? Where do responsibilities sit when an incident affects users across several services?

NewsBTC recently examined the operational requirements of tokenised securities venues, where ownership records and corporate actions remain essential despite the appeal of blockchain settlement.

Coinbase’s new presentation shows how major crypto platforms are positioning themselves as end-to-end service providers rather than standalone exchanges. Whether that gives issuers better outcomes will depend on transparency, competition and the performance of the services after the marketing presentation ends.

#5218. Elliptic Traces $124M in Bitcoin Swaps From Binance Hack Funds

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: A November 6 update from blockchain intelligence firm Elliptic says roughly $124 million of assets stolen in the October Binance breach had been converted into Bitcoin, including funds originally held as XRP and SOL. Onchain tracing can reveal movement, but it cannot by itself identify every person controlling those wallets or prove that all the converted funds have been cashed out.

The laundering trail from the huge October cryptocurrency theft attributed by investigators to North Korean-linked actors continues to evolve. In a November 6 update to its technical analysis, Elliptic said the value of stolen assets converted into Bitcoin had reached approximately $124 million.

The headline figure is striking, but the more useful story concerns how the funds moved, what remains traceable and why conversion into Bitcoin is not the same as spending money through the conventional financial system.

Elliptic’s investigation describes activity involving tens of thousands of wallets, multiple networks and an assortment of services. By its November 6 checkpoint, analysts had identified about 1,650 BTC held in new addresses following conversion from other stolen assets. The firm said roughly $50 million worth of XRP had begun moving largely towards Bitcoin, while stolen Solana tokens had also been swapped, bridged or mixed.

The firm presented this as an ongoing, rapidly changing investigation. An estimated figure tied to a timestamp should not be reported as a permanent total, and wallet clusters can change as further transactions occur.

Cross-chain movement complicates tracing because the deposit and payout sides of a transfer may occur on different networks. It can also make the trail harder to follow when funds pass through pools, aggregators and intermediaries. However, the public nature of blockchain transactions and the ability to connect wallet activity through known services can still help investigators reconstruct substantial portions of the flow.

Elliptic reported that approximately $2.85 billion of the original stolen assets had been frozen and about $3.11 billion remained in addresses linked to the theft at its latest checkpoint. The firm cautioned that only a negligible portion appeared to have been cashed out. Such estimates may change with later tracing, and asset values vary with market prices.

This matters because a criminal actor may hold large amounts of Bitcoin or Ether for some time before attempting to move value through brokers or exchanges. Public addresses can show coins being shuffled, but they generally cannot prove the real-world identity of each subsequent controller or the final ownership arrangement.

The distinction is especially relevant to compliance services. Screening against attributed addresses can alert businesses to potential sanctions or illicit-funds exposure, even when the funds have crossed networks. Yet address blacklists and automated risk scoring are not perfect substitutes for investigation and human judgement.

The evolving theft occurred alongside a different security incident affecting Chainalysis, another blockchain-analysis provider. The two incidents should not be conflated. Chainalysis described its own systems and credentials issue as unrelated to the Binance theft, while Elliptic’s work here concerns tracing funds from that separate exchange incident.

For operators, the lesson connects to the custody, counterparty and incident-response themes covered in NewsBTC’s reporting on digital-asset infrastructure restrictions. Protecting users involves controls over withdrawals, counterparties and incident communications — not simply watching one chain’s transaction explorer.

The next meaningful updates will concern verified freezes, attributed movements to identifiable services and evidence of actual cash-out. Elliptic’s data show the stolen funds are still moving through complex paths. They do not yet tell a complete story about who ultimately receives them or how much can be recovered.

David Schwartz, former chief technology officer of Ripple and one of the original XRP Ledger architects, has responded to claims that he is partially to blame for XRP's poor performance.

In a recent interaction on the X social media platform, David Schwartz was challenged about his possible impact on the price of the Ripple-linked cryptocurrency.

"Don't run from this. You can honestly say you don't have anything to do with it? It's not unfounded anger," the user wrote.

Although David Schwartz does not entirely deny that he can have an impact on the price of XRP, he is clear that it is minimal.

"Can I honestly say that I have nothing to do with the price of XRP? I guess probably not nothing. But very little," David Schwartz responded.

The response from Schwartz comes in the wake of mounting anger within the XRP community about the token's long-running price slump.

Indeed, XRP has seen roughly a 50% decline in value over the past year, per data from CoinMarketCap. During this period, the token has seen several temporary spikes, but the overall trend has been downward.

Of course, XRP is not the only token experiencing such a dramatic drop in value.

Stellar (XLM), another prominent cryptocurrency that seeks to enable payments, has seen a very similar price trend over the same time period.

The interaction came on the back of a long post in which Schwartz lamented the rise in hostile replies he receives on X.

Schwartz, a Ripple veteran, disclosed that some users are actually following him into other discussions and then proceeding to either label him a fraud or criticize him for his work on XRP.

The Ripple veteran noted that he has now made the decision to block such users, as irrelevant crypto-related posts are disrupting his discussions with other users.

Nonetheless, he stressed that the decision affects both critics and fans. Even if someone makes a positive comment about XRP but in an unsuitable place, they might also get blocked.

He also emphasized that he has no issue with honest criticism or accusations that make sense and come with good arguments.

He is mostly annoyed with users who keep hijacking unrelated discussions to vent their frustration.

In fact, Schwartz even offered to unblock users who commit to not doing so in the future.

Schwartz stepped away from his day-to-day duties at Ripple at the end of 2025. He had worked at the firm for over a decade. However, he has not completely left Ripple.

Earlier this month, Schwartz clarified that he's still on Ripple's board of directors and holds the honorary title of CTO Emeritus.

Furthermore, he disclosed that he still meets with his old team twice a month.

#5214. Aave Buys Avon Team to Bring More Fixed-Rate Lending Onchain

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Aave Labs said November 6 it had acquired Avon’s team and technology, including fixed- and floating-rate lending systems and an onchain order book. The move adds expertise for fixed-rate borrowing, but does not mean a finished fixed-rate Aave product has launched for every user.

Most people who take out a conventional loan want a clear answer to one question: what interest rate will they pay over the borrowing period? Decentralised finance often works differently, with interest rates that vary as supply and demand change within a lending pool. Aave Labs wants to broaden that model and has taken a new step towards it.

In its November 6 acquisition announcement, the company said it had bought the team and technology behind Avon, a developer focused on fixed-rate and floating-rate lending markets. The transaction includes Avon’s onchain order book, protocols, domains and other related assets. Financial terms were not disclosed.

The Aave release says Avon engineers Prince Sinha and Ayush Kaul will join the engineering team, while Omar el-Ashaal will join business development. Their stated focus includes fixed-rate lending and new types of onchain credit products.

A fixed rate can help borrowers plan expenses and hedge uncertainty. But supplying a dependable fixed-rate loan onchain requires more than setting a number at origination. Liquidity must be available over the loan’s term, interest-rate risk has to be allocated, collateral can change in value and lenders must be compensated for taking duration and credit-related risks.

Avon’s order-book technology could be relevant because an order book offers a different way to match borrowing and lending preferences compared with a purely pool-based floating-rate market. The acquisition does not itself prove that a design has completed security audits, won any required governance approval or become accessible to ordinary customers.

Aave describes itself as the largest onchain lending network, reporting more than $33 billion of deposits and $13 billion of active loans in its announcement. Those figures are company-reported and can fluctuate with token prices, collateral flows and market conditions.

The project already supports variable-rate borrowing and multiple asset markets. NewsBTC recently covered Aave’s protective freeze on new tBTC borrowing and supply, a reminder that risk settings and asset-specific decisions remain important even on an automated lending platform.

Fixed-rate capability could be useful to fintech partners and institutions that want more predictable liability management. It could also introduce complexities around maturity dates, rates, early repayment and liquidation that need careful contract design.

Aave Labs builds products that interact with the broader Aave network, but governance and the status of each deployed market matter. The acquisition is a corporate development and an engineering investment, not a guarantee that a new borrowing market is live today or approved across jurisdictions.

In NewsBTC’s prior reporting on Aave’s first externally curated V4 markets, the responsibility for risk settings and the structure of individual lending markets emerged as central questions. Fixed-rate lending will face similar scrutiny.

What should users watch for next? Published product specifications, audited contracts, governance decisions, clear rate and repayment terms, and evidence of sustainable liquidity. Aave’s acquisition explains the direction of travel: bringing more familiar credit-market features onchain. Whether users get the predictability they expect will depend on how those features are actually designed and deployed.

#5211. Solana Labs-Backed Leap Launches Beta App for Tokenized Stocks and Crypto

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Leap, described by Solana Labs as a mobile trading app for tokenised stocks, ETFs, metals, currencies and crypto, launched in early-access beta on iOS on November 5. The app brings several asset categories into one interface, but each token’s legal rights and user eligibility still need separate examination.

Solana’s tokenised-asset ambitions are moving into another consumer-facing interface. In a November 5 announcement distributed by Solana Labs, Leap said it had launched an early-access iOS beta app for trading multiple kinds of assets represented onchain.

The offering brings tokenised stocks and exchange-traded funds alongside metals, currencies and cryptocurrencies, with the stated goal of providing market context, clearer execution and detailed profit-and-loss tracking. Leap says it was built by the team behind Dialect.

Putting assets in the same app can make switching between markets easier for users, but the underlying instruments may remain quite different. A conventional listed share, a tokenised entitlement to a share, a cryptocurrency and a claim linked to a commodity can involve different legal rights, custodians and market hours.

The announcement should therefore be read as an application launch, not proof that every listed security has been made directly transferable to every wallet or that all asset classes operate under identical rules.

NewsBTC examined the NYSE’s planned tokenised securities infrastructure, highlighting the importance of transfer agents, corporate actions and investor rights. Those questions still matter when trading takes place through a polished phone screen rather than an institutional desk.

Leap’s November 5 release describes early access on iOS, not unrestricted public availability across all devices and countries. Beta launches allow developers to test user experience and market integrations, but they also mean functionality, supported regions and service rules can change.

The company highlights informed trading, market information and precise P&L presentation. Those features can help users understand orders, yet the accuracy of a dashboard depends on price feeds, cost-basis tracking and the availability of underlying markets. A clear interface is a benefit only if it communicates the risks, fees and settlement terms faithfully.

Liquidity also deserves attention. A tokenised equity can be technically transferable on a blockchain while the market for it remains thin. Bid-ask spreads, redemption arrangements and the ability to exit positions can differ from the traditional market in the underlying asset.

The wider Solana ecosystem has been expanding its settlement and tokenised-market infrastructure. NewsBTC’s reporting on Solana’s delivery-versus-payment tool examines the institutional side of this effort. Leap is attempting to bring related activity to a consumer trading experience.

That does not by itself guarantee meaningful network revenue or token demand. App adoption should be measured through active users, actual trades, repeat usage and transparent liquidity conditions, rather than the breadth of assets named in a launch release.

The next useful disclosures will be supported jurisdictions, precise asset rights, custody arrangements, fee schedules, trading hours and the move from beta to wider distribution. Leap has put a new interface in users’ hands. The larger test is whether the financial products behind that interface are as clear and dependable as the app aims to be.

A mysterious $163,000 crypto transaction has fueled rumors that Roger Ver, the controversial Bitcoin evangelist also known as 'Bitcoin Jesus,' may be purchasing Bitcoin Cash (BCH) once more.

According to on-chain analytics platform Onchain Lens, 73.31 Ethereum (ETH) coins were recently swapped for around 655.74 BCH coins (around $163,000) with the help of the decentralized cross-chain protocol THORChain.

Ver was famously an avid proponent of BCH, hailing it as a better option than the original Bitcoin network.

Ver, a crypto pioneer who first entered the crypto space in 2011, quickly rose to become one of the most recognizable early Bitcoin advocates.

He was so passionate about the digital asset that he even earned the moniker 'Bitcoin Jesus' for his aggressive promotion of the cryptocurrency.

But as Bitcoin's controversial scaling debate (which ultimately saw the birth of Bitcoin Cash in August 2017) kicked off, Ver's relations with Bitcoin's mainstream community took a hit.

Ver quickly emerged as one of Bitcoin Cash's most vocal champions.

He passionately argued that BCH's larger block sizes and lower fees help keep Bitcoin true to its roots as a peer-to-peer electronic cash system.

For the past year, Roger Ver has been in the news mostly due to his well-publicized legal dispute with the U.S. government.

Back in April 2024, the crypto entrepreneur was arrested in Spain after U.S. authorities accused him of failing to pay roughly $48M in taxes on his massive Bitcoin holdings and transactions.

Ver, who renounced his U.S. citizenship back in 2014, insisted the prosecution was unjust.

He persistently tried to poke holes in the government's argument.

In June 2025, Ver upped the ante even further.

He took Spain to the European Court of Human Rights to contest the country's decision to extradite him to the U.S.

But the feud took a bombshell twist in October 2025.

Ver and the U.S. Justice Department reached a settlement through a deferred prosecution agreement.

The cryptocurrency figure agreed to pay almost $50 million in unpaid taxes, penalties, and interest.

#5207. Kraken Parent Payward Takes AAVE Stake as Institutions Look Deeper Into DeFi

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Payward, the infrastructure company behind Kraken, said November 5 that an affiliated fund and its clients had acquired an undisclosed amount of AAVE through secondary markets. The investment signals interest in decentralised credit, but no stake size or binding future partnership terms were provided.

A major centralised crypto platform is putting capital behind one of decentralised finance’s best-known governance tokens. In a November 5 statement, Payward said Digital Asset Special Investments I, an affiliated fund, and its clients acquired an undisclosed amount of AAVE, the native token of the Aave lending network.

The purchase is notable because it gives an institutionally connected group financial exposure to an onchain protocol without the announcement describing an acquisition of the protocol itself. Aave remains a tokenholder-governed network, with its own governance mechanisms and smart contracts.

Payward said the tokens were bought in secondary-market transactions. It may make additional purchases, but did not disclose a stake percentage, a purchase price or a guaranteed future investment schedule. Without those details, it is impossible to judge the size of the position relative to AAVE’s circulating supply or to draw conclusions about voting control.

The company describes the investment as part of its asset-management activities and its view that onchain credit markets will have a larger financial role. That is a statement of commercial conviction, not evidence that Payward has obtained managerial authority over Aave’s software or the ability to direct every lending market.

AAVE holders can participate in governance according to the network’s rules. However, owning a token is not the same as holding shares in Aave Labs or having a claim on profits in the conventional corporate sense. The rights attached to a governance token need to be assessed from the protocol’s actual rules and proposals.

Traditional finance businesses have several ways to engage with decentralised lending. They can buy tokens, provide liquidity, integrate loan services or build products for clients. Each route carries distinct risks around smart contracts, pricing, regulatory compliance and custody.

Payward’s announcement references the Aave network’s substantial deposits and borrowing activity. That scale can make a protocol interesting to established firms, but total value locked is not the same as annual profit or guaranteed protection against loss. NewsBTC has previously examined Aave’s operational controls around tBTC exposure, showing that a large system still needs to manage asset-specific dependencies.

The company also cited opportunities for future collaboration, while leaving their exact form open. Investors should resist turning exploratory language into a signed distribution partnership, an exclusive product arrangement or a guaranteed inflow of institutional capital.

If Payward eventually introduces additional Aave-related services for its customers, the details will matter more than the token purchase alone. Customer eligibility, loan terms, collateral handling, software audits and safeguards against liquidation all affect the usefulness of any integrated product.

NewsBTC’s coverage of Aave V4’s externally curated lending markets provides an example of how protocol design assigns responsibilities to specific risk managers, rather than treating all DeFi lending as one uniform product.

The next milestones are formal details of any joint initiatives, disclosures about the fund’s AAVE exposure where required, and evidence of customers using integrated services. Payward’s acquisition of tokens is a confirmed step, and an interesting one. It does not tell us in advance whether DeFi’s credit infrastructure will become part of mainstream financial distribution at scale.

Crypto industry is dealing with another security turmoil, as a breach at Web3Auth, the wallet authentication infrastructure owned by Consensys, has exposed private keys of certain Keplr wallets, according to the official statement of TrustWallet representative on X.

The November 7 incident led to emergency service suspensions and recovery efforts, which could add pressure to an already fragile crypto market.

Web3Auth confirmed that a security issue in its infrastructure had compromised certain embedded wallets integrated with Keplr, especially accounts created through Google or Apple login.

Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery estimates that attackers drained at least $6 million from more than 44,000 wallets.

Those wallets sit across eight Cosmos ecosystem networks, including Cosmos Hub, Osmosis, Celestia and Injective.

Keplr warned users from depositing into compromised accounts and Web3Auth on their side suspended embedded wallet service, actively working on a recovery of vulnerable assets.

MetaMask stated that there is no evidence of affected users, though the situation is still under control. Trust Wallet has been unaffected, says its representative Felix. The impact on other third-party integrations is yet to be confirmed.

On October 29, Binance reportedly suffered a massive security breach involving around $6.3 billion, while Bitget was hit by an exploit estimated at $387.5 million in September.

Earlier in 2026, KelpDAO lost around $290 million after an exploit involving cross-chain infrastructure.

DeFi protocols, wallet infrastructures, smart contracts: those kinds of incidents are relevant for almost every project on the market. Exploits directly affect market sentiment, investors losses and safety in the industry in general.

Projects that rely on embedded wallet technology and Cosmos-related assets have unfortunately been affected directly and repeated security failures might damage their market picture state even further.

Luckily, there's no proven link between the Web3Auth expoit and declines on the market as a whole, including assets like Bitcoin and Ethereum. The investigations and rapid protocol patches are being released after more than 24 hours since the discovery.

#5202. Morpho loan stress exposes cbXRP, but spares native XRP

A Nov. 6 snapshot placed 8.84 million USDC across 1,070 positions within a further 10% oracle decline, assuming unchanged debt and collateral.

A 10% decline from the collateral price recorded around 13:24 UTC on Nov. 6 would make positions carrying about 8.84 million USDC of debt eligible for liquidation in a Morpho lending market on Base.

The snapshot covered 1,070 positions borrowing USDC against cbXRP, Coinbase's XRP-backed token. A smaller 5% decline would bring 462 of those positions, carrying about 3.23 million USDC of debt, to or beyond the same boundary.

For XRP holders who borrow against their tokens, further price weakness creates a choice between repaying debt, committing more collateral, or facing liquidation. Borrowing preserves exposure to the asset, while adding a financial obligation that becomes harder to support as collateral loses value.

Coinbase describes cbXRP as a wrapped token backed 1:1 by native XRP held in its custody. A holder can use an existing XRP position as collateral, so rising loan balances alone do not create new XRP purchases.

At 13:24 UTC, the market carried about 59.2 million USDC of total debt against roughly 119.9 million cbXRP in collateral. The debt inside the further-10% stress bucket represented approximately 15% of that borrowing, and the affected positions held about 12.73 million cbXRP.

Conditional exposure in one Base cbXRP/USDC market, using November 6 positions with debt and collateral quantities held fixed.

An illustrative 60% starting LTV rises to 66.7% when collateral value falls 10%, leaving debt and collateral quantities unchanged.

At the same lower oracle price, repaying 10% of original debt restores the illustrative position to 60% LTV.

Adding about 11.1% to original collateral quantity at the lower oracle price restores 60% LTV.

The 5% group sits inside the 10% group. Repayments or added collateral can change the outcome.

The market's oracle, the price feed used to value collateral, uses Chainlink's XRP/USD feed with a fixed 1:1 USDC leg, and its reported ratio was about 1.1843 USDC per cbXRP.

Borrower actions can change the exposed balance before prices reach either scenario.

Consider a position starting at 60% LTV. A 10% fall in the oracle price, with debt and collateral quantities unchanged, raises its LTV to about 66.7%, beyond this market's 62.5% threshold.

Repaying 10% of the debt would restore the original 60% LTV at the lower price. Adding about 11.1% to the original collateral quantity would achieve the same result, excluding interest, fees, and further price moves.

The market interface recorded repayments and collateral additions around 13:14-13:16 UTC on Nov. 6. Those transactions show that positions were changing around the observation window.

For borrowers using Coinbase's interface to Morpho on Base, optional automatic collateral protection can add assets after a configured trigger. Borrowers must enable it and have assets available, and volatility or technical problems can prevent execution.

That makes the fixed-position estimate sensitive to both borrower responses and whether intended top-ups actually complete.

Once a position becomes eligible, an external liquidator can repay some or all of its debt and receive collateral plus an incentive. In this market, that exchanges USDC debt repayment for cbXRP collateral.

The exposed positions hold 12.7 million cbXRP, but the amount actually seized depends on subsequent liquidation transactions.

A liquidator may retain or trade that collateral, and any resulting native-XRP sales would require separate evidence linking the liquidation to those sales.

For holders using XRP-backed credit, the immediate pressure is to keep debt supported as collateral values change. Subsequent repayments, collateral additions and executed liquidations will determine how much of this snapshot's exposure remains.

#5201. Ripple's XRP Ledger Lending to Receive Repayment Fix

The XRP Ledger's lending protocol is in for a tidy-up of how loan repayments get rounded. In plain terms, the balance after each payment would match the schedule, the update has been discribed in the official Github pull request.

After an overpayment, TotalValueOutstanding is reset to the scheduled value of the new PeriodicPayment.

Under the LendingProtocolV1_2 amendment, each on-time LoanPay would bring TotalValueOutstanding down to the scheduled value with one payment fewer, capped at the rounded PeriodicPayment.

The first commit moves the scheduled-value calculation out of computeLoanProperties into a separate scheduledValue function, with no behavior change.

That way, LoanSet and LoanPay round it the same way. Zero-interest loans also need a floor on the principal part, because their value is rounded to nearest while the principal is rounded up. Tests run on Legacy, CashBasis and FixedPrecision vaults, with and without the amendment.

Today, each payment's value part is calculated on its own, so rounding can build up across payments. The last payment can then need one unit more than the rounded PeriodicPayment, and the value parts can alternate between payments.

With the change, a method called telescoping makes the value part of every on-time payment either the floor or the ceiling of PeriodicPayment, and at least one unit. The last payment becomes exactly the rounded PeriodicPayment.

There's little to no effect for users and investors today. The extra unit on the final payment changes little. Older loans that already carried one unit above their schedule simply keep it, so the last payment still needs the PeriodicPayment and a single unit, unless the borrower overpays first.

Small overpayments are mostly ignored; the transaction goes through successfully and charges no extra XRP whatsoever.

Activation date is yet to be determined: 80% of validators agreement is needed for two weeks in a row for the amendment to go through. No public vote for LendingProtocolV1_2 has been announced yet, so the timeline remains uncertain.

#5200. Google Tells Schools They Can Reject AI—But They'll Lose Search, Too

Google Tells Schools They Can Reject AI—But They'll Lose Search, Too

Google is giving schools more freedom to reject artificial intelligence—provided they're also willing to give up Google Search, which is arguably what everybody in the world uses Google for.

The company announced Tuesday that its AI products will be disabled by default for K-12 student accounts unless administrators explicitly enable them. But schools that want to ban AI entirely will also have to disable Google's search engine, a tool millions of students rely on for everyday research.

Chris Phillips, Google's vice president and general manager of education, tried to justify the reasoning during a meeting with educators.

“Search and AI are deeply integrated,” he said according to Education Week. Schools uncomfortable with AI can choose not to enable Search at all.

Google says administrators will be able to activate or disable Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Search individually. That means schools can block the standalone chatbots while keeping Search available, but they cannot remove AI from Search itself.

For teachers who want students to research sources without receiving AI-generated answers, the company is effectively offering two options: accept its AI-powered search or find another search engine.

The announcement is already drawing accusations that Google is using its dominance in education to push a technology many schools are still trying to understand, regulate or restrict.

Google says the changes are intended to address concerns that AI chatbots can undermine learning by giving students ready-made answers instead of encouraging them to solve problems themselves.

Beginning in early 2027, schools that enable Search will be offered versions with conventional AI features, such as AI Overviews and AI Mode, or the education-focused Guided Learning experience, according to The New York Times.

Neither option provides the traditional search experience without generative AI.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani accused the company of “trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” according to CBS News.

Former Federal Trade Commission chair Lina Khan was equally critical, accusing Google of using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting AI.

The criticism comes as some of America's largest school districts are actively restricting generative AI. New York City, for example, imposed a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI through eighth grade, covering nearly 600,000 students, while Los Angeles has also restricted the technology.

Los Angeles officials had specifically hoped to preserve Google Search while removing AI-generated summaries. Under the newly announced controls, that won't be an option.

Google's position also arrives amid continuing antitrust scrutiny. A federal court ruled in 2024 that Google unlawfully monopolized the U.S. search market, and the company has faced separate legal challenges over its decision to integrate AI summaries into search results.

School administrators are expected to receive the new controls in early 2027. They will be able to decide which AI products students can access, and even apply different settings by grade level. A Google Search option without AI, however, is not among the choices.

That said, for schools that want to, ahem, unofficially ban AI without losing Google search, our guide may provide a quick solution. It takes 5 minutes and lasts forever.

#5199. Bitcoin erases post-election gains as Wall Street selloff triggers over $1 billion in crypto liquidations

Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here.

The selloff triggered a wave of forced liquidations across crypto derivatives markets, as total liquidations over the past 24 hours reached $1.09 billion, affecting 211,000 traders.

Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other cryptocurrencies erased their post-election gains on Thursday as a sharp selloff in U.S. technology and AI stocks spilled into cryptocurrency markets, triggering more than $1 billion in leveraged position liquidations over the past 24 hours.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell 6% to $75,700, after touching an intraday low of $75,568, while ether (ETH) dropped more than 7% to $2,247. The declines reversed Wednesday's rally, when bitcoin climbed back above $80,000 following the U.S. midterm elections and signs that the Binance hack had not caused broader market disruption.

Midterm election results appeared to generate short-term optimism, but analysts say they haven't resolved macroeconomic uncertainties.

As of 2 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 were down about 3% for the day, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite had dropped 4.7%. The Cboe Volatility Index, or VIX, surged approximately 60%, reflecting heightened investor anxiety.

AI and bitcoin-related mining stocks were among the hardest hit, with Bitdeer and Keel Infrastructure each falling about 20%. American Bitcoin dropped 17% despite announcing a quarterly profit of $126 million. Crypto bellwethers Strategy and Coinbase were each down about 10%.

Of note, the Official Trump (TRUMP) memecoin hit an all-time low after falling more than 20% over the past two days.

The selloff also triggered a wave of forced liquidations across crypto derivatives markets. About $879.92 million in positions were liquidated over a four-hour period, including $818.90 million in longs and $61.02 million in shorts, according to CoinGlass. Total liquidations over the past 24 hours reached nearly $1.1 billion, affecting nearly 211,000 traders.

It should be noted that liquidation figures are typically based on publicly available data, which may significantly understate the extent of market liquidations.

The reversal suggests Wednesday's rebound may have been driven more by temporary optimism than a meaningful improvement in the market's underlying conditions, according to Wintermute.

The trading firm said the rally reflected a combination of relief following the Binance hack, enthusiasm surrounding the election results, optimism about a potential slowdown in AI spending and falling oil prices. However, those factors proved short-lived as broader macroeconomic pressures persisted.

"It's probably a combination of all of them in some way. What matters is that all of them seemed to be so short-lived that it actually didn't really matter," said Jasper De Maere, an OTC trader at Wintermute. "Trump is still the president for two years, the Middle East is still escalating, inflation is elevated into a strong U.S. economy."

Beyond the immediate market pressures, the election results may also complicate the outlook for crypto regulation, potentially tempering some of the optimism that helped drive Wednesday's rebound.

Paul Howard, senior director at Wincent, said the Democrats' strengthened position in Congress could make bipartisan cooperation necessary for meaningful progress on crypto legislation over the next two years. With the Clarity Act's prospects uncertain, Howard expects the existing regulatory framework to largely remain intact until the next election cycle.

Ryan Kirkley, CEO of Global Settlement Network, said the election could delay crypto legislation but wouldn't fundamentally change longer-term institutional demand for digital assets.

"Investors are still focused on liquidity, interest rates and the broader economy, and those factors will continue to influence the market regardless of which party controls Congress," Kirkley said.

If the weakness continues, Wintermute identified $73,000 and $68,000 as the next levels to watch for bitcoin. The firm said it would need to see bitcoin convincingly reclaim and hold $80,000 before turning more positive.

An anonymous Tornado Cash whale sent $7 million to Hyperliquid to open a large long on Bitcoin this morning. According to Lookonchain and Onchain Lens, the wallet went in with aggressive 20x leverage with the plan to profit from Bitcoin crushing Ether.

Large holders usually run funds through mixers to move capital privately or to get ready to cash out. This case is unusual as the movement of these funds had just previously been tracked to a chain of addresses belonging to the hackers who drained the derivatives platform Drift Protocol of $290 million in April 2026.

Some blockchain researchers warn against jumping to conclusions about where the funds came from. There's still no direct evidence: Tornado Cash covers its tracks well, and the link between the wallet and specific hacks rests only on circumstantial matches in volume.

After starting as a brand-new address that withdrew 3,100 ETH from Tornado Cash, the unknown later swapped all of the Ether through CoW Swap on the spot, locking in $6.92 million in USDC. From there, the money went to the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid as collateral for future trades.

On the exchange, the whale didn't try to guess where the market was headed and just split the collateral in half, turned on 20x cross leverage and built a position worth about $26 million in total. The position consisted of $12.84 million at an entry price of $75,762.2 and an Ethereum short of 5,740 ETH worth $12.83 million.

So far, the bet is working. Bitcoin is holding near local highs, and the gain on the BTC long fully covers the drawdown from altcoin short. Add to this the earnings on funding, collecting a regular premium from other traders for holding the ETH short.

This is a textbook dominance pair trade, where the investor couldn't care less whether the industry as a whole goes up or down and the only thing that matters is the spread - the price gap between the two largest coins.

If Bitcoin rises faster than Ether, or if Ether falls harder than Bitcoin in a broad market crash, the trade profits.

The math is elegant, but 20x leverage is always a high risk. Should Ethereum rip higher while Bitcoin stays stuck in a range, the margin will be wiped out in seconds as Hyperliquid's cross-margin system will force-close the orders, and the investor will lose the entire $6.92 million. The liquidation price is set at $37,014.09 for BTC and $3,343.60 for ETH.

#5197. Stablecoin contraction forces Bitcoin drop despite Fed reserve gains

The dated comparison pairs a reserve rebound with shrinking dollar-token circulation, leaving the link to Bitcoin buying unestablished.

Bank reserve balances rose $67.5 billion between Oct. 28 and Nov. 4, according to the Federal Reserve’s Nov. 5 release, but the more abundant dollar liquidity is not automatically bullish for Bitcoin.

Over the same period, data provider DefiLlama tracked dollar-pegged stablecoin circulation falling by more than 5.7 billion units, or 1.91%.

The split leaves an incomplete picture for a Bitcoin recovery. Higher bank reserve balances would still need to translate into financing and purchases, so the measured token contraction adds a crypto-side observation to that test.

A Nov. 5 Treasury-cash analysis considered a possible December funding window using projected cash paths and the older Oct. 28 reserve baseline. The new release updates that starting point with a rebound in realized reserves.

Coinbase's completed Nov. 5 daily BTC-USD candle closed at $75,969.06, down 5.54% from $80,428.31 on Nov. 4. That close-to-close fall followed the dated reserve observation, putting the price move outside the bank-balance comparison window.

The Fed’s H.4.1 release puts Nov. 4 reserve balances at $2.96 trillion. Over the preceding week, the Treasury General Account, the government’s account at the Fed, fell $79.4 billion to $936.2 billion.

Treasury payments move balances into depository institutions’ accounts, increasing reserves all else equal, while receipts flowing into Treasury’s account work in the opposite direction.

The final reserve change also incorporates movements elsewhere on the Fed’s balance sheet. Total assets rose $2.5 billion, while other balance-sheet changes offset part of the effect of the Treasury-account drawdown.

Tether’s USDT series fell 3.65 billion units, accounting for 63.37% of that measured contraction, while USD Coin (USDC) circulation declined 383 million units, contributing 6.64%. Other tracked dollar-pegged tokens together contracted a net 1.73 billion units.

The issuer breakdown locates the largest measured change in USDT. Whether, and to what extent, issuer redemptions, bridge-accounting adjustments, reclassification, or coverage revisions contributed remains unquantified.

#5194. Hyperliquid Strategies files to become CFTC-registered FCM, posts $13.3 million in quaterly revenue

Get The Block’s latest crypto news and price alerts for the coins you follow, right in Chrome. Add our free extension here.

The filing would let the HYPE treasury firm carry U.S. client accounts for HIP-3 perpetual futures markets, pending regulatory approval.

Nasdaq-listed Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR) reported $13.3 million in revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30, exceeding analyst estimates of $10.6 million to $12 million, depending on the data provider.

The company posted $620.6 million in net income, largely driven by $803 million in unrealized gains on its Hyperliquid (HYPE) token holdings, partially offset by a $172.3 million income tax provision.

Perhaps most notably, Hyperliquid Strategies filed with the CFTC to become a futures commission merchant (FCM), which would allow the firm to carry U.S. client accounts for HIP-3 markets.

"Hyperliquid recently announced its intention to add additional deployer functionalities under the name HIP-3," the firm said in a release. "These optional additional features would allow deployers to build and launch permissioned markets on Hyperliquid's onchain infrastructure. Independent operators would run their own market in a compliant manner, while the chain underneath would stay a neutral infrastructure layer."

The FCM, which is subject to regulatory approval, would allow Hyperliquid Strategies to "play a role" in bringing perpetual futures to U.S. customers within a regulated framework.

"There can be no assurance as to the timing or outcome of the application or regulatory approval of permissioned HIP-3 markets," the firm said.

This comes as Hyperliquid's underlying infrastructure moves closer to the U.S. market. NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange agreed last week to partner with TradeXYZ to bring Hyperliquid-based perp futures markets to U.S. traders. ICE would operate the exchange and clearing infrastructure, with TradeXYZ designing the markets.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump said his administration was working to bring Hyperliquid into the U.S. "in a fully compliant and legal fashion."

#5193. MEXC sees $126 million outflows as US targets exchange over $16.7 billion in suspected illicit transactions

MEXC says trading remains normal and customer assets are secure, but the Treasury's latest action could complicate its banking relationships.

Crypto exchange MEXC saw $126 million in net outflows as US regulators moved to sever its access to the American financial system.

The withdrawals coincided with a Nov. 6 enforcement action by the Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), which accused the exchange of facilitating $16.7 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion, terrorist financing and cybercrime.

Data from DeFiLlama showed $126.03 million in net outflows over a 24-hour period spanning the announcement, while the exchange retained approximately $4.353 billion in tracked assets.

This represent net movements through monitored wallets and do not establish that all withdrawals occurred after the announcement or indicate whether the exchange has sufficient assets to meet its customer liabilities.

MEXC has moved to contain concerns about its financial position, insisting that customer funds remain secure and its trading, deposit and withdrawal services are operating normally.

In an official statement, the exchange said it was reviewing the Treasury order with its legal and compliance teams and had initiated an independent examination of its anti-money laundering and sanctions controls.

“We take the concerns raised seriously and intend to engage constructively with FinCEN, as well as other relevant regulators and competent authorities worldwide.”

CEO Vugar Usi separately sought to clarify the implications of the order after concerns spread among users.

“A number of misconceptions are floating around,” Usi said, emphasizing that the restrictions apply to transactions involving US financial institutions rather than the exchange's entire global operation.

“The order itself does not freeze or seize any assets held on MEXC. Users can trade normally.”

Usi expressed confidence that the matter would be resolved and said the exchange would continue updating customers as discussions with regulators progress.

The response followed a sweeping investigation that identified significant deficiencies in MEXC's compliance controls despite its stated policies against servicing customers in sanctioned jurisdictions.

In its 24-page order, FinCEN said MEXC facilitated approximately $16.7 billion in likely illicit activity between May 2021 and May 2026, including transactions involving Russian sanctions evasion networks and Iranian-linked entities.

Nearly $1.5 billion involved direct or indirect exposure to Russian sanctions evasion, including $232 million in direct dealings with sanctioned entities.

FinCEN specifically identified approximately $129 million in transactions involving Garantex and another $4.1 million involving Grinex after the Russian exchanges were sanctioned by Western authorities.

The agency said MEXC continued transacting with both exchanges as recently as June 2026.

Investigators also identified more than $1.87 billion in transactions with Iranian exposure, including approximately $1 billion in direct transfers involving more than 40 Iranian crypto exchanges.

Another $22 million involved Iran's central bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, including its Qods Force.

Separately, the agency identified at least $1.99 billion involving illicit cyber actors, including more than $37.9 million in suspected ransomware payments.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent framed the enforcement action as part of Washington's broader effort to restrict financial channels used by sanctioned actors. He said:

“Either you support the Iranian regime, or you have access to the U.S. financial system.”

The order prohibits covered US financial institutions from sending or receiving funds involving MEXC, including cryptocurrency transfers, beginning 30 days after its publication in the Federal Register.

It has no scheduled expiration date, although FinCEN retains the authority to grant exemptions.

The restriction does not shut down MEXC internationally or automatically freeze customer assets, but it could complicate the exchange's relationships with banks, financial intermediaries and liquidity providers that operate within the US regulatory system.

The US enforcement action comes as MEXC retreats from several international markets amid mounting regulatory scrutiny, even as its trading business continues to expand.

As CryptoSlate reported on Oct. 30, the exchange has announced withdrawals from France, the Netherlands, Russia and Belarus as part of its efforts to address compliance concerns.

The latest US intervention adds to those setbacks, potentially complicating MEXC's ambitions to expand beyond cryptocurrency trading into traditional financial markets.

The regulatory pressure comes despite the exchange's growing market presence.

A TokenInsight report showed that MEXC processed $1.069 trillion in trading volume during the third quarter of 2026, ranking fourth among exchanges covered by the study.

Its overall market share reached 8.91%, up 0.38 percentage points from the previous quarter.

MEXC has also gained ground in derivatives linked to traditional financial assets, processing $86 billion in commodity perpetual futures during the quarter. That gave it a 17.43% market share, second only to Binance.

The figures highlight the scale of the trading business now exposed to heightened regulatory uncertainty as MEXC attempts to broaden its presence in global financial markets.

Although FinCEN's order does not prohibit MEXC from operating internationally, it could disrupt relationships with banks, liquidity providers and other intermediaries subject to US jurisdiction.

The extent of that disruption remains unclear because MEXC has not disclosed how much of its trading activity or liquidity depends on institutions covered by the prohibition.

The immediate test will come when the restrictions take effect, particularly whether the exchange can maintain its existing financial relationships while addressing the compliance deficiencies identified by US authorities.

#5192. ChatGPT Is Getting a GIF Maker Powered by OpenAI's Unannounced Images 2.6 Model

ChatGPT Is Getting a GIF Maker Powered by OpenAI's Unannounced Images 2.6 Model

The internet may soon have an unlimited supply of AI-generated dancing cats, courtesy of ChatGPT.

OpenAI is rolling out a feature that lets users generate animated GIFs directly inside ChatGPT, according to The Verge. The feature reportedly comes powered by its new image-generation model called Images 2.6, which OpenAI has yet to formally introduce through its usual product announcements.

Users can describe an animation in plain English or upload an existing photo and ask ChatGPT to bring it to life. Once the GIF is generated, they can adjust its playback speed, inspect individual frames, make edits, and share the finished animation.

OpenAI demonstrated the capability with a simple request: “can you make a gif of a cat dancing?” The resulting interface reportedly includes controls to change animation speed and examine the GIF frame by frame.

We tried generating GIFs using ChatGPT, but the feature was not available on our accounts at the time of testing. In our interaction, the model generates a series of frames, but not the animation.

The rollout appears to be gradual, so users may have to keep asking for their dancing cats a little longer.

The GIF maker is reportedly part of a broader Images 2.6 update that promises faster image generation. The Verge reports that OpenAI is bringing the model to ChatGPT and Codex users across web, desktop, and mobile platforms.

Developers are also getting two new API models, GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and GPT-Image-2.6 Sunburst, designed for faster generation and higher-quality results, respectively. OpenAI has not yet published a standalone announcement detailing the new model's capabilities, and we could not independently test its performance.

The update follows the September release of ChatGPT Images 2.5, which introduced sharper details, more precise editing, and generation speeds up to 50% faster than its predecessor.

In our previous testing, Images 2.5 went head-to-head with Google's Nano Banana 2 across six categories, with each model winning three. OpenAI's model delivered particularly impressive illustration quality and improved on the oversharpening problems that affected earlier versions, although it still made mistakes when rendering text.

The move into GIF generation also comes months after OpenAI shut down Sora, its standalone AI video-generation app, in March. Animated GIFs are considerably simpler than the videos Sora generated, but the new feature brings a form of motion generation directly into ChatGPT without requiring a separate application.

OpenAI has not provided a specific date for when every ChatGPT account will receive GIF generation.

#5190. Best Crypto-Friendly Banks: 5 Options for Crypto Investors and Businesses

Home » Cryptopedia » Best Crypto-Friendly Banks: 5 Options for Crypto Investors and Businesses

Which banks will support your crypto habits?

Finding a crypto-friendly bank in 2026 is not as simple as opening an account with a traditional financial institution. Some banks allow transfers to cryptocurrency exchanges like Coinbase, while others offer built-in crypto trading, digital asset custody, or specialized banking services for Web3 businesses.

The best option depends on where you live, whether you are an individual investor or a crypto business, and which digital asset services you need. Some providers also impose restrictions on specific exchanges, transaction limits, or crypto-related business activities.

In this guide, we compare crypto-friendly banks and fintech providers, examining their supported services, availability, fees, and limitations to help you find the right banking solution in 2026.

A crypto-friendly bank makes it easier for individuals and businesses to interact with the cryptocurrency market through traditional financial services. Depending on the provider, this may include allowing transfers to and from crypto exchanges, offering crypto trading or payment features, or providing banking services to eligible crypto companies.

Not all crypto-friendly providers offer the same features. Some let customers buy, sell, and hold digital assets directly, while others simply support transfers to selected platforms like Kraken or provide financial services to Web3 businesses. Some are licensed banks, while others are fintech companies that partner with banks to deliver their services.

Before exploring the best crypto-friendly banks, consider the main advantages and potential drawbacks.

If you’re looking for the best crypto-friendly bank to join in 2023, you’re in the right place! This list breaks down some of the top banks for cryptocurrency from a variety of fields, including traditional banking, business banking, and personal accounts.

Revolut remains one of the more accessible options for people who want to manage traditional money and cryptocurrency through a single financial app.

Revolut is a digital banking platform that combines traditional financial services with cryptocurrency features. In supported markets, customers can use its app to buy, sell, hold, and transfer cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin and Ethereum. Available assets and features depend on the customer’s country and account eligibility.

Revolut also supports crypto withdrawals and deposits through selected external wallets and blockchain networks. However, transaction fees, supported assets, and withdrawal limits vary. Its cryptocurrency services are provided by separate legal entities from its banking services, and crypto holdings are not covered by standard bank deposit protection.

Wirex flips the script amongst the other ‘best crypto-friendly banks’ contenders. While other platforms began their story as traditional banks and slowly moved to cryptocurrency acceptance, Wirex set out to be the world’s leading crypto bank from day one.

Wirex is a global fintech platform combining traditional currencies, cryptocurrency services, and payment cards. Users in eligible markets can buy, sell, exchange, and hold supported digital assets, as well as use available payment services to spend their funds.

Wirex also hosts a cross-chain bridge, offers crypto-linked cards, and a Cryptoback rewards programme, which advertises rewards of up to 8% on eligible purchases.

Actual rewards depend on the card programme, subscription, and applicable conditions. Wirex is not a traditional bank; its services are provided through regulated entities and financial partners, depending on the customer’s location.

Mercury is a US-based financial technology company providing business banking services through partner banks. It is particularly relevant to eligible cryptocurrency and Web3 startups, DAOs, and investment funds that need traditional financial infrastructure to manage their operations.

Businesses can use Mercury to manage fiat deposits, payments, expenses, and transfers to supported cryptocurrency exchanges, including Coinbase and Gemini. However, Mercury does not hold cryptocurrencies or provide crypto trading services.

It supports most eligible US-registered businesses, including those founded by international entrepreneurs, but does not accept applications from crypto exchanges or money services businesses.

Monzo is a UK-based digital bank that allows customers to use their accounts with selected cryptocurrency exchanges.

Although it does not offer native cryptocurrency trading, customers can transfer money to supported platforms, including Coinbase, making it an option for investors who want to manage traditional banking and crypto purchases separately.

Monzo applies transaction monitoring and restrictions to cryptocurrency-related payments. For example, it currently blocks payments to Binance while allowing transfers to a range of other exchanges. Its cryptocurrency payment allowance is also limited, so customers should check the latest terms before making large transactions.

Ally Bank is a US-based digital bank offering traditional banking products, including checking accounts, savings accounts, and investment services. Unlike specialist crypto-friendly financial platforms, Ally does not provide direct cryptocurrency trading or cryptocurrency custody through its banking services.

Customers cannot transfer cryptocurrencies directly to Ally accounts, which accept transactions in US dollars. Ally Invest also does not currently support direct cryptocurrency trading, although customers can access certain crypto-related investment products, including cryptocurrency funds and publicly traded companies involved in the industry.

Ally is therefore better suited to customers looking for conventional banking and investment services rather than direct access to cryptocurrency exchanges or digital assets.

Choosing a crypto-friendly bank involves more than finding a financial institution that allows cryptocurrency transactions. The right option depends on your location, investment activities, and whether you need basic exchange transfers or more advanced crypto-related services.

Here are five important factors to consider:

Check whether the bank supports transfers to your preferred cryptocurrency exchanges, such as Coinbase, Kraken, or Binance. Some financial institutions restrict payments to specific platforms or apply additional security checks to crypto-related transactions.

Compare account maintenance fees, international transfer costs, currency conversion charges, and any limits on cryptocurrency-related payments. Some providers also charge separate fees for buying, selling, or withdrawing digital assets.

Look for providers with appropriate regulatory authorisation and transparent security policies. Check whether eligible fiat deposits are covered by a recognised deposit guarantee scheme and understand that cryptocurrency holdings generally receive different protections.

Crypto-related banking services are not available everywhere. Before opening an account, check whether the provider accepts customers in your country and whether its cryptocurrency features are accessible in your region.

If you operate a Web3 startup, blockchain company, or cryptocurrency-related business, check the provider’s business eligibility requirements. Some platforms, including Mercury, support eligible technology and Web3 companies but exclude certain activities, such as operating a cryptocurrency exchange or money services business.

Crypto-friendly banks and financial platforms make it easier to manage traditional money and cryptocurrency in one place. However, their safety depends on regulation, banking partnerships, and security measures.

An important distinction is that eligible fiat deposits may be protected by deposit guarantee schemes, while cryptocurrencies generally are not. Crypto assets also carry risks such as market volatility, custody issues, and potential losses.

Not every crypto-friendly platform is a licensed bank. Providers such as Wirex and Mercury may operate through regulated entities or partner banks. Before choosing one, check its licences, account terms, and what protections actually apply to your funds.

Several financial institutions and fintech platforms support cryptocurrency-related transactions. Revolut and Wirex offer crypto services in eligible markets, while Monzo supports transfers to selected cryptocurrency exchanges. Mercury provides banking services to eligible Web3 businesses, whereas Ally Bank primarily offers traditional banking and investment products.

The best option depends on your needs. Revolut is suitable for individuals seeking integrated crypto services, Wirex focuses on cryptocurrency payments and spending, and Mercury caters to eligible Web3 businesses. Monzo can be useful for UK customers transferring money to supported exchanges.

Yes, many banks and financial platforms allow transfers to Coinbase, although availability depends on the customer’s location, payment method, and account restrictions. Always check your bank’s current cryptocurrency payment policy and Coinbase’s supported funding methods before initiating a transfer.

Yes. Banks can restrict or decline cryptocurrency-related payments for security, fraud prevention, regulatory compliance, or internal risk-management reasons. Some institutions also block transactions involving specific exchanges. Customers should review their provider’s terms and conditions before making crypto-related transfers.

Eligible deposits held with licensed banks may be covered by national deposit protection schemes, depending on the institution, account type, and applicable limits. However, cryptocurrency holdings are generally not covered by traditional bank deposit insurance. Fintech platforms may also use partner banks, so customers should identify the institution actually holding their deposits and verify the applicable protection.
